title: Riff-Diff Hybrid Diffusion Designs De Novo Enzymes Rivaling Directed Evolution
whyItMatters: Published in Nature: scaffolds catalytic motifs into de novo proteins for retro-aldol and Morita–Baylis–Hillman reactions, achieving activities rivaling in vitro evolution with exquisite stereoselectivity.
summary: Researchers at Graz University of Technology and the University of Graz introduced Riff-Diff (Rotamer Inverted Fragment Finder–Diffusion) in Nature, combining atomistic catalytic-motif geometry with generative protein diffusion to scaffold custom active sites from scratch without massive experimental screening campaigns. Demonstrated across two mechanistically distinct organic synthesis reactions—the retro-aldol and Morita–Baylis–Hillman reactions—Riff-Diff produced de novo biocatalysts matching catalytic efficiencies previously attainable only after rounds of directed evolution, with six high-resolution crystal structures confirming near-atomic active-site precision.
technicalHighlights: Hybridizes atomistic rotamer-motif scaffolding with generative protein diffusion to position multi-residue catalytic arrays at sub-angstrom accuracy.
Delivered de novo catalysts for both retro-aldol and Morita–Baylis–Hillman chemistry rivaling directed-evolution activity with high stereoselectivity.
Six high-resolution X-ray crystal structures confirmed near-atomic agreement between designed and experimental active sites.
caveats: Catalytic turnover still depends on carefully specified quantum-chemical transition-state geometries (theozymes); industrial-scale thermal/solvent stability remains target-dependent.

scoreRationale.foundational: Overcomes the historic weak-activity bottleneck of computational enzyme design, matching directed-evolution efficiencies out of the box.
scoreRationale.ripple: Opens general-purpose green biocatalysis for non-natural organic synthesis across pharmaceuticals and fine chemicals.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature with kinetic assays, stereoselectivity measurements, and six high-resolution experimental crystal structures.
scoreRationale.velocity: Replaces large-library random mutagenesis campaigns with direct computational generation of high-activity enzymes.

sources.label: Braun, Tripp, Oberdorfer et al. — Computational enzyme design by catalytic motif scaffolding (Nature, 2025/2026)
